strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates that uniform reasoning length introduces redundancy across heterogeneously difficult substeps
Practical lightweight design: single-model serving with on-the-fly LoRA strength adjustment avoids multi-model coordination overhead and enables efficient KV-cache reuse
Comprehensive experiments across multiple scales: three models (QwQ-32B, Qwen3-14B/8B), three benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME24), and five baselines, showing consistent 30-47% token reduction
Clear presentation with intuitive motivation and effective qualitative examples (Figure 4) illustrating how MixReasoning avoids verbose traces
Interesting technical finding (Finding 3): layerwise ablation showing reasoning path length is governed by MLPs rather than attention, enabling further optimization for full KV-cache reuse
Reproducible: detailed implementation settings, training hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics provided
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core components are largely combinations of existing techniques (LoRA distillation from Ma et al. 2025b, token entropy from Wang et al. 2025b, mode switching conceptually similar to speculative decoding); main contribution is engineering rather than fundamental innovation

Entropy-based triggering insufficiently validated: (1) paper acknowledges heuristic 'does not learn end-to-end' and 'can be sensitive to calibration and non-local dependencies' (A.1); (2) no empirical validation that token entropy correlates with decision criticality; (3) no error analysis of failure cases; (4) requires tuning three hyperparameters (τ↑, τ↓, window size) without principled guidance

Training-test distribution mismatch: LoRA adapter trained only on GSM8K (7.47k simple problems) but evaluated on harder MATH-500 and AIME24; no ablation comparing per-benchmark adapted models; potential confound where simpler training distribution may help more than reported

Missing baseline comparisons and statistical rigor: several baselines missing for QwQ-32B (DEER, NoWait, ConciseHint); no explanation provided; results averaged over only 5 runs with no confidence intervals or significance testing

Efficiency claims not fully supported: wall-clock latency not measured; prefill overhead only mentioned casually ('roughly 1-2 tokens worth') without quantification; claims about 'substantially improves efficiency' lack concrete latency data

Limited qualitative analysis: only one example per model; U-shaped accuracy trend in Figure 3 mentioned but not explained; claims about 'verbosity-induced errors' lack supporting evidence; no problem-category analysis
Narrow evaluation scope: only mathematical reasoning tested; no evaluation on other domains (commonsense, code); AIME24 has only 30 problems; unclear scaling to harder problems
Readability claims unvalidated: claims about 'more human-readable' responses lack human evaluation; only qualitative examples provided
Hyperparameter sensitivity only analyzed on GSM8K: Figure 3 sensitivity shown only for one benchmark; unclear if hyperparameters transfer across datasets
Incomplete ablations: no ablation on hysteresis mechanism (τ↑ vs. τ↓), window components (B vs. F), or interaction with LoRA strength values (α_low vs. α_high)

strengths: Well-motivated core insight: adaptive reasoning depth is a natural and useful solution to redundancy in long chains-of-thought, positioned clearly against both uniform compression and problem-level hybrid routing

Technically sound and practical design: single-model LoRA-based switching avoids multi-model coordination overhead while providing explicit control knobs (window size, entropy threshold) for per-request adjustment

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks, multiple model scales, and five representative baselines with consistent Pareto frontier improvements (e.g., 47% token reduction + accuracy gain on GSM8K)
Valuable ablation insight (Finding 3): demonstrating that reasoning length is governed by MLPs rather than attention K/V has practical implications for future optimization strategies
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and qualitative examples that convincingly demonstrate where and why the method allocates reasoning effort
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging that entropy-based triggering is heuristic and can be sensitive to calibration, with transparent discussion of future work directions
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines well-established components (LoRA, token entropy signals) in an incremental rather than foundational way; individual technical contributions are not novel

Heuristic uncertainty triggering without learned alternatives: entropy-based approach acknowledged to not learn end-to-end; no comparison with learned policies (RL/imitation learning); sensitivity to model calibration unexplored

Significant generalization concerns: LoRA trained exclusively on GSM8K which has atypically short ground-truth rationales; no evaluation on non-mathematical domains (common sense, scientific reasoning, code generation) raises questions about transfer

Missing experimental comparisons: baselines marked with '–' without explanation (DEER, NoWait, ConciseHint on QwQ-32B); no empirical evaluation against cited hybrid reasoning methods; no wall-clock latency measurements, only token counts

Insufficient hyperparameter analysis: multiple hyperparameters (α_low, α_high, τ↑, τ↓, B, F) with limited sensitivity analysis and no practitioner guidance for setting values across different problems/models

KV-cache reuse claims inadequately substantiated: prefill overhead claimed as 'small' without quantification; proposed MLP-only LoRA for full reuse mentioned but not empirically demonstrated; no actual latency validation

Reproducibility gaps: no code availability mentioned, windowed regeneration procedure under-specified, exact extraction/prompt details sparse, results reported without confidence intervals or significance testing
Limited failure analysis: no investigation of when entropy-based triggering fails, which problem classes degrade, or systematic error analysis; no ablation on entropy threshold choices
Statistical rigor concerns: some accuracy differences marginal (0.9612 vs 0.9613); no significance testing provided; results averaged over only 5 runs

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: clearly articulates limitations of uniform compression (underthinking) and instance-level routing (misses within-problem heterogeneity)
Elegant technical design: LoRA adapter strength control enables fine-grained mode switching while preserving base model capability and avoiding catastrophic forgetting
Rigorous theoretical foundation: Appendix C.1 provides formal analysis showing token confidence is reverse-KL concentration measure (Proposition C.1) with monotonicity guarantees
Comprehensive empirical validation: 4 models × 4 benchmarks with consistent 13-49% token reduction and maintained/improved accuracy; thorough ablations on design choices
Practical efficiency demonstrated: End-to-end latency improvements (Figure 6) show token savings translate to wall-clock speedups; KV-cache reuse analyzed quantitatively
Strong experimental design: 5 independent runs reported; comparisons with 6 baselines; Pass@k analysis demonstrates robustness beyond Pass@1; extended evaluation on code and commonsense reasoning
Clear presentation: Excellent motivating figures (1-3), precise algorithm (Algorithm 1), qualitative examples with explicit mode highlights (Appendix D), and honest limitation discussion
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Combines three established components (LoRA, token confidence, hysteresis control) in novel way but lacks fundamental algorithmic innovation

Critical adapter quality bottleneck: Table 5 shows concise adapter drops from 64.67% to 27.99% on AIME24 even with 300K training examples; method depends on strong base model + quality training data + proper difficulty detection—three-way dependency limits generalization

Incomplete switching overhead analysis: Appendix C.3 is theoretical; empirical overhead not separately reported; Figure 6 conflates token reduction with switching gains; rollback frequency and impact unmeasured despite being central mechanism (Eq. 5)

Threshold tuning not fully systematic: τ_low sensitivity only studied on Math500 (Figure 5); τ_high = τ_low + 2 appears arbitrary without justification; while Figure 4 shows distribution stability, this doesn't guarantee transfer to new domains
Insufficient concurrent work comparison: AlphaOne and AdaptThink addressing similar adaptive reasoning control mentioned but minimally compared; weakens novelty claims

Missing experimental details: No confidence intervals/significance tests despite reported variance; top-k parameter (k=20) not ablated; dwell time distributions not analyzed; cross-model adapter transfer not tested
Generalization concerns: Evaluation primarily on STEM/math tasks; training data from model-specific non-thinking outputs; no evidence of transfer across models or domains beyond appendix extensions

Incomplete design justifications: Window size m=16 selected from single-benchmark sensitivity analysis; no comparison of aggregation methods beyond sliding-window average; semantic connection between window size and reasoning units not formalized
No failure mode analysis: Paper doesn't discuss problems where early difficult steps are critical; mode-switching errors not characterized; only success cases shown

Reproducibility gaps: Code link stated as 'available here' but no actual URL provided; requires special access to proprietary models; deployment complexity not quantified (batching efficiency, memory overhead vs. baseline)
